text:
nisha: Hey all  quick question on hosted vs sandbox keys during my first week. I'm doing streaming tests and keep getting 429s when I switch to the hosted key from the sandbox key. Is there a different flow for hosted keys locally?

sam: Welcome! You should be able to call hosted directly from your laptop. 429s can be rate-limit or concurrency. What does the error payload show?

nisha: Just shows \"rate_limited\" and a generic message. I'm running several parallel streaming curls while iterating on client code.

devon: Streaming counts as an open connection for rate limiting. Sandbox has low burst/concurrency to avoid abuse. Hosted is higher but still has per-account/route limits. For dev iterate use the sandbox with a small concurrency or the local dev-proxy to record and replay.

nisha: Hmm ok. If I want CI to run integration tests, is it OK to use hosted key in CI? worried about leaking into forks/PRs.

maria: Don't put long-lived hosted keys in PRs or public forks. Use a scoped CI token (read-only) or sandbox key for PR runs. For deploys on main, use a short-lived hosted token injected via repo secrets.

sam: Another pattern: record golden responses with the proxy in the PR pipeline, then have a smaller smoke test that hits hosted only on the main branch. Saves quota and reduces flaky 429s.

nisha: Can you show the GitHub Actions snippet you mentioned?

sam: Sure, example we use:```yamlname: CIon: pull_request:branches: [main]jobs:build:runs-on: ubuntu-lateststeps:- name: Run tests  env: REDWOOD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}  run: |    if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]; then      export KEY=${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}    else      export KEY=${{ secrets.REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY }}    fi    ./scripts/run-integration.sh```Keep hosted key only in secrets and restrict secrets access to workflows on main.

devon: For local proxy, simple curl:```bash# start proxy locallyhttp://localhost:8080/v1/generate# call via proxycurl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY" -d '{"model":"gpt-open-1","input":"hi"}' http://localhost:8080/v1/generate# direct hostedcurl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"model":"gpt-open-1","input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate```

nisha: Nice. How do I request higher sandbox quota if I need more parallel streams for testing?

maria: Ping <@devex> with numbers (conns, rps, time window) and team/use case. They usually grant temporary boosts for onboarding and demos. If urgent open a support ticket and tag sandbox-quota.

devex-bot: Note: sandbox quota requests typically take 1-2 business days. For emergency onboarding needs DM the devex lead.

nisha: Last thing: what env var names should I standardize on?

sam: We use REDWOOD_API_KEY for hosted, REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY for sandbox, REDWOOD_PROXY_URL for local proxy. Rotate hosted keys regularly and prefer short-lived tokens for CI deploys.

nisha: Thanks everyone! I'll switch to proxy + sandbox for PRs and file a quota request if needed. :thumbsup:
